title: Continuous Concepts Removal in Text-to-image Diffusion Models

summary: The public routine fixes one calibration prompt per call, compares denoisers at different states, and cannot independently initialize original teacher and previous-stage student. Its removal loss and final genetic selection also differ from the paper. These are release-to-method discrepancies, with original experiment effects unresolved.
impact_rationale: Minor: all five supported findings concern the public realization of the method. Their exact local counterexamples do not establish which implementation generated the published diffusion-model results.

problems.title: One fixed prompt does not cover the calibration set within a training call
problems.source_location: Sections 4.1–4.3, PDF pp.4–7; train-scripts/train-ccrt.py, lines 127–133 and 192–199
claim: The calibration-set procedure is implemented by choosing one random entity before the training loop and repeatedly reusing it.
analysis: For two non-target prompts with student responses \((\theta_1,\theta_2)\) and zero teacher responses, set removal loss \(\mu|\theta_2-1|\), \(\mu=1/200\), and preservation weight \(\lambda=1/100\). Fixing the first prompt minimizes \(\mu|\theta_2-1|+\lambda\theta_1^2\) at \((0,1)\). Uniform full-set preservation instead adds \(\lambda(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)/2\), whose minimizer is \((0,1/2)\). Randomizing a single anchor across calls is not the same adaptive trajectory as resampling within a call.
result: The release provides single-anchor training, not within-call set coverage. An external anchor schedule could be intentional; Eq.(4) alone does not specify a sampling law.
repair: If empirical-set preservation is intended, resample the calibration prompt each step or use a minibatch average. Otherwise document single-anchor training and its schedule. The usual conditional expectation of a sampled fixed-state gradient then equals the empirical-set gradient.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded public sampling/objective correspondence issue, not measured loss of full-model alignment.

problems.title: Common starting noise does not give a common latent argument
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, Eq.(4), PDF p.4; train-scripts/train-ccrt.py, lines 214–225; ldm/models/diffusion/ddim.py, lines 239–259
claim: Eq.(4) compares teacher and student at one \(x_t\). The release independently samples their latent states before comparing predictions.
analysis: A valid zero-noise DDIM step with cumulative coefficients \(\alpha=1/5\), \(\alpha_{\rm next}=4/5\) has form \(z_{\rm next}=2z-b\epsilon(z)\), \(b=3/\sqrt5\). Start both at \(z=1\), use teacher \(\epsilon_*(z)=z\), and student \(\epsilon_\theta(z)=kz\), \(k=2/b-1\). Their states become \(z_*=2-b\) and \(z_\theta=b\). The cross-state residual is \(kb-(2-b)=0\), but the common-teacher-state squared residual is \((k-1)^2(2-b)^2\approx0.112422373>0\).
result: The implemented zero discrepancy need not mean zero common-input discrepancy. A trajectory-level objective may still be useful but is a different objective.
repair: Choose and disclose one latent-sampling rule, then evaluate both denoisers on exactly the same latent, time and prompt. Freeze the teacher and treat sampling consistently with the intended gradients.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact witness isolates a released objective mismatch; its empirical size and historical use are unknown.

problems.title: One checkpoint path cannot specify both later-stage initializations
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF pp.4–5; Section 4.3, p.7; train-scripts/train-ccrt.py, get_models, lines 99–106
claim: A later stage requires original teacher \(\theta_0\) and student initialized at \(\theta_{i-1}\). Both public loader calls instead receive the same checkpoint path.
analysis: For \(\theta_{i-1}\ne\theta_0\), no single supplied path realizes the required ordered pair. Loading the previous model moves the teacher; loading the original restarts the student. The objectives differ concretely: retained responses \(f_i=i\delta\), \(\delta=0.1\), have previous-stage discrepancy \(0.01\), but original-reference discrepancy \(0.25\) at stage \(5\). This is an exact reference distinction, not a claimed observed model trajectory.
result: The release cannot independently express the described continuous original-teacher procedure. An unpublished wrapper or different generating revision could resolve historical correspondence.
repair: Expose separate original-teacher and student-initialization checkpoint arguments and retain their identities in each stage record. They may coincide at the first stage.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a released initialization interface limitation; it does not establish that published stages used the wrong teacher.

problems.title: The released squared removal loss differs from the stated absolute norm
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, Eq.(3), PDF p.4; train-scripts/train-ccrt.py, lines 185 and 225–229
claim: The paper explicitly uses the residual \(\ell_1\) norm; the public routine instantiates MSELoss for both removal and alignment.
analysis: For a scalar removal target \(1\), retained target zero and \(\lambda=1/100\), the paper-form objective is \(J_1(x)=|x-1|+x^2/100\), uniquely minimized at \(1\). The squared version \(J_2(x)=(x-1)^2+x^2/100\) is minimized at \(100/101\). At that point \(J_1=201/10201>1/100=J_1(1)\). Scalar dimension removes any mean-versus-sum explanation.
result: The two losses can optimize different solutions. Which loss produced each original experiment is unresolved.
repair: Use the stated absolute norm with an explicit reduction convention, or document the squared objective and identify its generating runs. Changing the norm also changes relative weighting in higher dimensions.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a public loss-to-description discrepancy, without a demonstrated empirical reversal.

problems.title: The returned genetic population need not be a scored elitist union
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, Algorithm 1, PDF p.6, lines 11–13; eval-scripts/generate-entity.py, lines 233–299
claim: The paper selects the best members of the parent/offspring union. The release scores and truncates before variation, then may terminate after unscored replacements.
analysis: Let \(k=2\) and fitnesses \(F(a)=3\), \(F(b)=2\), \(F(c)=1\), \(F(d)=0\). In an allowed no-crossover realization, initial scoring retains \((a,b)\); mutation removes \(a\) and creates \(d\). Population size is still \(2\), so the loop exits and returns \((b,d)\) without evaluating \(d\). Elitist union selection from unchanged parents and that offspring instead returns \((a,b)\). This traces an allowed control-flow realization, not its frequency in default runs.
result: The public finalization does not enforce the declared selection property. It does not establish global genetic-search failure or quantify generated-prompt quality.
repair: Keep unchanged parent records, score every new genotype, and apply \(\operatorname{Top}_k(E_j\cup O_j;F)\) after variation on every return path. Its finite union-selection property follows directly from ordering the compared scores.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local public selection-logic discrepancy with unknown historical calibration-set effects.
